remarks.name: Guillermo Rauch
remarks.role: vercel CEO
remarks.text:
Super bullish on WebMCP. Much like Tesla FSD meets the world where it is (streets, stoplights, potholes and all), agents *need* to ride the existing WWW infrastructure… WebMCP makes it more efficient.

Some pretty unique wins too. e.g: Next.js dev pages could expose debugging tools directly to agents in the specific tab they’re testing, with page-specific context, instead of sifting through server logs. No separate MCP server to find and configure because the page directly exposes its own 'agent tools'.

e.g: in this world 𝚏𝚡 + 𝚊𝚐𝚎𝚗𝚝-𝚋𝚛𝚘𝚠𝚜𝚎𝚛 is a complete web dev stack with zero loss in debugging depth
remarks.translation: 超级看好WebMCP。就像特斯拉FSD是在现实世界中运行（街道、红绿灯、坑洼全都得应对），智能体*必须*依托现有的WWW基础设施……WebMCP让它更高效。还有一些相当独特的优势。例如：Next.js开发页面可以直接向正在测试的特定标签页中的智能体暴露调试工具，并提供页面专属上下文，而不必翻查服务器日志。无需寻找和配置单独的MCP服务器，因为页面直接暴露了自己的“智能体工具”。例如：在这个世界里，𝚏𝚡 + 𝚊𝚐𝚎𝚗𝚝-𝚋𝚛𝚘𝚠𝚜𝚎𝚛就是一个完整的Web开发技术栈，调试深度零损失。

remarks.name: Madhu Guru
remarks.role: Sr Director, AI at Meta; Prev: Google - Led Gemini, Veo, Nano Banana.
remarks.text:
Here’s one practical thing you can do this weekend to get better at building AI products.

Pick a workflow you know well - from your personal life or your work.

Automate the whole thing with AI.

Use the AI product you’re comfortable with - you’ll probably have to experiment with a few.

This exercise will force you to think about

1/ What does a great end-to-end experience look like?
2/ How should you use MCPs and tools?
3/ Where should humans stay in the loop?
4/ How do you evaluate it?

Then keep expanding the ambition.

You’ll learn more by doing this once than by reading about AI product building for a month.

The only way to learn is to build.
remarks.translation: 这个周末，你可以做一件很实际的事，让自己更擅长构建AI产品。挑一个你非常熟悉的工作流程——无论是来自个人生活还是工作。用AI把整个流程自动化。使用你用得顺手的AI产品——你可能需要多试几个。这个练习会迫使你思考：1/ 一个出色的端到端体验应该是什么样？2/ 你应该如何使用MCP和工具？3/ 哪些环节应该保留人工参与？4/ 你如何评估它？然后不断扩展你的目标。做一次这件事，比读一个月关于AI产品构建的内容学到的东西更多。学习的唯一途径就是动手构建。

podcasts.originalExcerpt: A few years ago, Caltech Prof. and co-founder of Accelerated Understanding, Anima Anandkumar set out to develop the first open-source weather model with AI. Talking to experts in the field, she was met with skepticism. Weather is chaotic, physics simulations are hard, have been developed for decades, and require supercomputers, the data just isn’t there. Despite reservations, Anima went forth and built. Within a year her team had developed FourCastNet, a predictive model that is competitive with the best physics-based simulations available. Thanks to Anima, and her follow up work, anyone can now predict weather accurately over a short timescale using consumer grade GPUs.
